timeline: You are standing yards away from the President when a rogue torpedo heads straight for your hull on November 14, 1943.
A Fletcher-class destroyer had just launched a real weapon during a routine drill.
President Franklin Roosevelt was aboard the battleship for a wartime conference.
Radio silence orders forced the panicked crew to signal with a lamp instead.
They messed up the message and told the flagship they were backing away instead.
Finally breaking radio silence, the destroyer screamed a frantic warning across the water.
The giant battleship turned hard, spinning away just in time to dodge the impact.
Roosevelt asked his Secret Service guard to wheel him closer so he could watch.
Three thousand yards away, the stray torpedo finally detonated in the ship wake.
From that day on, navy ships greeted the clumsy crew with one sarcastic joke.
You are aboard the USS Iowa on November 14, 1943, when a live torpedo fired by your own escort ship heads straight for your hull.
